title: Which backend owns the lock?
why: PostgreSQL and managed workspaces differ from standard remote backends.

title: Is the local Terraform process still active?
summary: Local state locks belong to the local process and cannot be force-unlocked by another process.
why: The safe recovery path is to identify the owning process, not use terraform force-unlock.

commands.purpose: Confirm the intended local workspace before retrying.

title: Allow the local operation to finish safely
summary: Do not start a competing local operation or remove lock artifacts blindly.
why: The lock protects the local state while the owning process is active.

choices.label: Process ended but lock symptom remains

title: Retry only after the local owner has ended
summary: Local state cannot be unlocked with terraform force-unlock; retry after confirming no Terraform process is active.
why: A persistent local lock symptom may indicate an orphaned process, permissions problem, or incorrect working directory that needs owner review.

commands.purpose: Retry bounded lock acquisition without disabling locking.

title: Is another remote-backend operation active?
summary: Check terminals, CI, remote runs and lock-owner metadata.
why: Removing a valid lock can permit concurrent state writes.

commands.purpose: Retry for a bounded duration without disabling locking.

choices.label: No active run and stale evidence

title: Preserve the valid remote-backend lock
summary: Wait or coordinate with the remote operation owner.

title: Use managed workspace controls
summary: Inspect run and lock ownership in the platform.
why: CLI force-unlock is not automatically correct.

title: Preserve the active managed-workspace lock
summary: Wait or coordinate through the HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise workspace.
why: Managed workspace ownership and run status are authoritative for this lock.

choices.label: Authorized administrator confirms a stale lock

title: PostgreSQL uses session advisory locks
why: The PostgreSQL backend does not support terraform force-unlock.

title: Preserve the active PostgreSQL advisory lock
summary: Wait for or coordinate with the database session that owns the Terraform advisory lock.
why: PostgreSQL backend locks are session-native and force-unlock is not supported.

title: Are all force-unlock prerequisites proven?
summary: Confirm directory, backend, workspace, lock ID, ownership and recovery options.
why: Never force-unlock based only on elapsed time.

title: Force-unlock only the exact stale lock
summary: Remove protection only after proving no operation is active.
why: Wrong unlock can allow concurrent state mutation.
prerequisites: Confirm no local, CI or remote run.
rollback: Stop new runs and coordinate state recovery if competing activity appears.

commands.purpose: Use only the exact confirmed stale lock ID.

title: Use authorized managed unlock
summary: An authorized owner may remove a proven stale managed lock.
why: Managed platform audit and ownership remain authoritative.
rollback: Re-lock or pause runs if unexpected activity appears.

title: Verify normal locking
summary: Confirm the original symptom is resolved and remains stable.
verification: State is readable and locks normally.
No lock disabling or state editing used.

title: Lock recovery verified
summary: Recovery is verified; record cause and prevention work.
prevention: Keep ownership metadata and state history.

title: Escalate to the state/backend owner
summary: Preserve redacted lock message, backend, workspace, lock ID, operation, run status and Terraform version; never share state or credentials.
